# fastmind

An embodied-AI multi-agent framework with a Rust-native async **dual-loop architecture** — the Rust
implementation of [fastmind](https://github.com/kandada/fastmind) (Python version), targeting
**100% functional parity**. It is a from-scratch rewrite following Rust idioms — *not* a line-by-line
port of the Python code.

## Dual-loop architecture

FastMind is built around two concurrent loops inside the same `Session`, communicating through a shared
`State` blackboard:

- **LLM slow loop (System 2)** — event-driven, runs the state graph (planning, tool use, human-in-the-loop).
- **VLA fast loop (System 1)** — time-driven, scheduled by frequency, bypasses the graph (balance /
  navigation / emergency reactions that must not wait for the LLM).

## Core concepts

| Concept | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| **Graph** | nodes + edges + conditional routing + subgraphs; any node is `async (&mut State, &Event) -> NodeOutput` |
| **State** | the shared blackboard; namespaces like `llm/`, `vla/`, `world/` keep loops decoupled |
| **Event** | discrete, queued, push — wakes the slow loop |
| **Signal** | continuous, last-value cache, pull — sensors feed the bus |
| **VLA** | time-driven inference + N:M action-channel routing |
| **Perception** | cross-session scheduled loops / sensors / timers |
| **Interrupt** | human-in-the-loop: `interrupt` event → checkpoint → `resume` / `cancel` |

## Features

- **Dual loop**: VLA fast loop + LLM slow loop in one session, sharing `State`.
- **Event vs Signal**: `Event` (discrete, queued, push) vs `Signal` (continuous, last-value cache, pull).
- **State-graph orchestration**: conditional edges, router functions, subgraphs, cycle detection, `max_iterations`.
- **Multi-consumer stream**: `EventBuffer` append-only ring buffer with independent cursors.
- **Human-in-the-loop**: `interrupt` events, checkpoints, `resume`/`cancel` routing.
- **Tools**: compile-time OpenAI schema via `#[tool]`, `ToolNode`, `StreamingToolNode`.
- **VLA action routing**: N:M channel routing with per-action error isolation.
- **Perception loops**: cross-session scheduler, stream sources, timers, sensor manager.
- **Idempotency**: duplicate `event_id` skipped per session.
- **Declarative macros**: `#[tool]` `#[agent]` `#[signal]` `#[vla]` `#[vla_action]` `#[graph]` `#[perception]`.

## Quick start

Add `fastmind = "0.1"`, then:

```rust
use fastmind::{Event, EventType, FastMind, FastMindAPI, Graph, State};
use fastmind::futures::StreamExt;
use serde_json::json;

#[fastmind::agent(name = "chat")]
async fn chat(state: &mut State, event: &Event) {
    state.set("reply", json!("Hello!"));
    state.output().unwrap().append(
        Event::new(EventType::STREAM_END, json!({}), event.session_id.clone()),
    );
}

fn app() -> std::sync::Arc<FastMind> {
    let mut b = FastMind::builder();
    b.agent(chat_agent());
    let mut g = Graph::new();
    g.add_node("chat", fastmind::agent_node(b.agent_registry().get("chat").unwrap()));
    g.set_entry_point("chat");
    b.graph("main", g);
    b.build()
}

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() {
    let app = app();
    let api = FastMindAPI::new(app.app());
    api.start().await;

    api.push_event("u1", Event::new(EventType::USER_MESSAGE, json!({"text": "hi"}), "u1"), "main")
        .await
        .unwrap();

    let mut stream = api.stream_events("u1", None).unwrap();
    while let Some(ev) = stream.next().await {
        if ev.type_ == EventType::STREAM_END { break; }
    }

    let state = api.get_state("u1").await.unwrap();
    println!("{}", state.get("reply").unwrap());
    api.stop().await;
}
```

## Structure

```
src/
├── lib.rs       # re-exports + feature gates + node!/vla_fn! macros
├── builder.rs   # FastMind builder facade
├── *.rs         # core: event/state/graph/node/tool/signal/vla/perception/buffer/session/engine/app
├── runtime/     # tokio runtime wrapper, tracked tasks, graceful shutdown
├── api/         # FastMindAPI, event streaming, session queue
└── llm/         # optional (feature "llm"): OpenAI-compatible adapter
fastmind-macros/ # #[tool] #[agent] #[signal] #[vla] #[vla_action] #[graph] #[perception]
tests/           # all integration tests
examples/        # all examples
benches/         # criterion micro-benchmarks
```

## Examples

Run with `cargo run --example <name>`:

| Example | Demonstrates |
|---|---|
| `simple_chat` | basic agent + graph |
| `simple_chat_with_tool` | tool calls + conditional edges |
| `streaming_chat` | char-level streaming |
| `human_in_loop` | interrupt / resume |
| `perception_loop` | timer perception |
| `drone` | tools + sensor perception |
| `companion_bot` | emotion + tools |
| `humanoid_robot` | multi-tool agent |
| `sleep_assessment` | multi-stage + HITL |
| `comprehensive_assistant` | multi-node graph |
| `npc_vla` | dual-loop VLA + signals + perception |

## Testing

```bash
cargo test                        # unit + integration (LLM tests skipped)
cargo test --features llm         # includes real-LLM integration tests
cargo clippy --all-targets
cargo fmt --all
```

### Real-LLM integration tests

`tests/llm_integration.rs` (behind the `llm` feature) exercises a full ReAct loop
(agent → tool call → `ToolNode` → answer) against a real OpenAI-compatible API via
[`openai-client-rs`](https://crates.io/crates/openai-client-rs). Set the environment (never hardcode the key):

```bash
export LLM_API_KEY="..."
export LLM_API_URL="https://api.deepseek.com/v1"   # optional, default
export LLM_MODEL_NAME="deepseek-chat"              # optional, default

cargo test --features llm --test llm_integration -- --nocapture
```

When `LLM_API_KEY` is absent the LLM tests skip gracefully. See `.env.example`.
